title: Solar Storms
subtitle: When the Sun gets angry

description:
Episode 30 of a daily journey through the universe. 🌌
We ride a solar storm: billions of tons of charged gas, the May 2024 storm that brought auroras as far south as Mexico, the Carrington Event of 1859, and the Sun's 11-year cycle.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 31: Next stop, Venus. The hottest planet.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

#space #solarstorms #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Episode thirty. Next stop... solar storms.
Sometimes the Sun throws billions of tons of charged gas into space. It's called a coronal mass ejection.
segments.headline: Billions of tons, launched

segments.text: When it hits Earth, it lights up auroras. In May twenty twenty-four, a huge storm painted the sky pink and red as far south as Mexico.
segments.headline: Auroras over Mexico, 2024

segments.text: The biggest storm on record, the Carrington Event of eighteen fifty-nine, set telegraph wires sparking.
A storm that strong today could damage satellites and knock out power grids.
segments.headline: Satellites and power grids at risk

segments.text: The Sun follows a cycle of about eleven years. We've just passed its most active phase.
Tomorrow, we visit the hottest planet. And no, it's not Mercury. Next stop: Venus. Follow, so you don't miss episode thirty-one.
